Verb Patterns · Questions at work · B2B customer service

Do you want that I check the stock?
Do you want me to check the stock?

Questions you ask business customers every day, and questions people ask about your job. Every question has two families: the letter builds the question, the number is the verb pattern.

Dotted is a work word you can learn. Passe o mouse ou toque para ver a tradução. Não é o foco da aula: o foco são as perguntas.

Primeiro, a sua opinião, dois números de verdade e uma conversa. Depois, dois aquecimentos para ver como as perguntas já saem. Depois, as perguntas sobre o seu trabalho e as perguntas que você faz ao cliente, com uma resposta modelo à mão. No fim, três armadilhas, três exercícios de ouvir e um role-play. O botão A B C Questions, no canto, abre a consulta das famílias a qualquer momento.

2Read

What can you trust?

Leia a matéria. As palavras com linha pontilhada têm tradução, e os números azuis levam às fontes
EIC · Neural EnglishCustomer service B2B
Feature · Customer service

The answer a customer can trust

31%of business buyers name inaccurate delivery times as a barrier to ordering online.1

Customers do not only want a fast reply. They want information that is correct, the same from every person, and reassuring.

EIC
About this textWritten for B1+ readers. The small blue numbers point to the sources on page 2. Words with a dotted line have a translation.

Correct

Ask a business buyer what goes wrong when ordering, and the answers are about information. In a 2024 survey of 1,000 buyers, the biggest barriers to ordering online were inaccurate delivery times (31%), inaccurate prices (29%), inaccurate stock levels (28%) and missing product information (28%).1

Figure 1 · Barriers to ordering online
Delivery times31%
Prices29%
Stock levels28%
Product information28%

Share of business buyers who named each barrier. Source: Sana Commerce survey, run by Sapio Research, 2024.1 Sana paid for the survey and sells software for B2B online stores. That does not make the numbers wrong, but it is a good reason to read other studies too.

The same survey found that buyers said 33% of their online orders had an error, up from 28% in 2019.1

The same from everyone

Information also has to match. In McKinsey’s 2026 survey of nearly 4,000 decision-makers in 13 countries, the top reasons for switching suppliers included inconsistent information across teams and no access to knowledgeable people.2

Think about what this means in a daily job. A date that is correct in the email but different in the system is not a correct date for the customer. Two people who give two answers create a doubt, and the customer has to decide who to believe.

1 | Read | Customer service B2BLevel B1+ · October 2026
EIC · Neural EnglishCustomer service B2B

Reassuring

In the 1980s, the researcher David Maister described how waiting feels.3 A wait feels longer when it is uncertain and when nobody explains it. Anxiety also makes a wait feel longer, and people are more anxious before service starts than while it is happening.

These are observations from practice, not results from a large survey. They match what many of us know from experience.

Compare two messages. The first: “We are checking.” The second: “We are checking with the warehouse. I will write to you by 3 p.m.” The second one gives a reason and a time. That is our example, not a result from a study.

Here is another imagined example. A buyer at a food factory knows her production line will stop on Friday if the enzymes do not arrive. Supplier A says, “It’s on the way.” Supplier B says, “There is a delay. The new date is Monday. Do you want us to send half of the order by air?” Supplier B gave bad news, but she did not have to chase anyone or guess.

On time

Speed still matters, and fast answers are rare. In 2011, three researchers sent a web inquiry to 2,241 US companies. Only 37% answered within an hour, 24% took more than a day, and 23% never answered. Among those that replied, the average reply took 42 hours.4

The companies that replied within an hour were nearly seven times more likely to qualify the lead than the others.4 A lead is a possible customer. This was a study of sales inquiries, not service requests, and the data is old, so we use it only as a sign of how rare a quick answer was.

Effort, and when things go wrong

A Harvard Business Review study of more than 75,000 customers, not only business ones, found that going above and beyond makes little difference. Customers mostly want a simple, quick solution.5 Salesforce asked 13,020 consumers and 3,916 business buyers, and 88% said the experience a company provides is as important as its products or services.6 That figure combines both groups.

When a failure happens, treatment matters. A 2021 study of 300 business customers of wholesalers in the hospitality industry found that fair treatment, and asking for the customer’s opinion during the recovery, led to more satisfaction.7 It was a small study in one industry, so we should not generalize.

What to do with this

These three ideas are our suggestions, based on the studies above.

  1. Check the date with the other team before you promise it.
  2. Give the customer a time and a reason, not only “we are checking.”
  3. Make sure your team gives the same information.

Speed is not always possible. A clear answer about the wait usually is.

References

  1. Sana Commerce B2B buyer survey, run by Sapio Research (1,000 buyers, six countries). Reported by Digital Commerce 360, March 2024.
  2. McKinsey, Global B2B Pulse, May 2026.
  3. Maister, D. (1985). The Psychology of Waiting Lines.
  4. Oldroyd, J., McElheran, K. and Elkington, D. (2011). The Short Life of Online Sales Leads. Harvard Business Review, 89(3), 28.
  5. Dixon, M., Freeman, K. and Toman, N. (2010). Stop Trying to Delight Your Customers. Harvard Business Review.
  6. Salesforce, State of the Connected Customer, 5th edition, May 2022.
  7. Oflaç, B., Sullivan, U. and Kaya Aslan, E. (2021). Journal of Business & Industrial Marketing.

5Your job

Questions about your job

O professor pergunta, você responde com a sua realidade. A resposta à mão é só um modelo
Aflip it × Family 1

Would you like customers to send you their forecasts earlier?

Definitely. I’d like them to send us a forecast every month, not just the purchase order.

Aflip it × Family 2

Can you make production change the plan for an urgent order?

Not really. I can’t make them change it, but I can ask supply chain to check.

Aflip it × Family 1com not

Have they ever told you not to promise delivery dates?

Yes. They told us never to confirm a date before supply chain approves it.

Badd it × Family 1

Does your manager ask you to call customers about delays?

Yes. She asks us to call them before we send the email.

Badd it × Family 2let

Does the system let you see the stock in real time?

Only for finished products. It doesn’t let us see what’s still in production.

Badd it × Family 2have

Do you have the warehouse confirm every shipment?

Yes. We have them confirm the pickup time with the carrier.

Badd it × Family 2make

Do delays at the port make you change delivery dates often?

Sometimes. One week at the port can make us push a delivery by ten days.

Cwh first × Family 1

What do customers usually ask you to send them?

They usually ask me to send the certificate of analysis and the technical data sheet.

Cwh first × Family 1

What does your company expect you to do when a shipment is late?

They expect us to tell the customer first, with a new date, before the customer has to ask.

Cwh first × Family 2

What does your company let you offer a customer when an order is late?

We can offer a partial shipment or air freight, but they don’t let us pay the extra cost without approval.

Cwh first × Family 3

What do you recommend that a customer do to avoid running out of enzymes?

I recommend that they send us a forecast and place orders at least eight weeks ahead.

Dkeep it × Family 1

Who taught you to use the order system?

My supervisor taught me. She showed me every screen in my first week.

Dkeep it × Family 2

What makes an order urgent for you?

When a customer’s production line will stop without our enzymes.

Dkeep it × Family 1

Who asks you to change orders at the last minute?

Usually the customer’s purchasing team. Sometimes they ask us to double the quantity a week before shipping.

Ehide it × Family 1

Do you know what your company wants you to improve this year?

Yes. They want us to answer every email within four hours.

Ehide it × Family 3

Can you tell me what supply chain suggested that you change?

They suggested that we confirm orders only after they check the stock.

Quick reference · consulta rápida
Question families
AFamily A · flip it · inverte
Já tem auxiliar na frase: be, can, will, would, should…
auxiliary + person + verb
Will your parents let you go?Seus pais vão te deixar ir?
Short answer: Yes, they will. Nunca entra “do”: Can you…?, não Do you can…?
BFamily B · add it · adiciona
Não tem auxiliar: entra do, does ou did.
do · does · did + person + base verb
Did she tell you to wait?Ela te mandou esperar?
O passado vai para o “did”: Did she tell, nunca Did she told. Short answer: Yes, she did.
CFamily C · wh first · palavra na frente
Você não sabe a ação, a coisa, o lugar: what, who, where na frente.
what · who · where + A or B
What do you want me to do?O que você quer que eu faça?
Depois do “what”, a pergunta é A ou B normal. Perguntando a ação, o “do” fica no fim.
DFamily D · keep it · não mexeLesson 2
O who ou o what é o sujeito: quem fez, o que causou.
who · what + verb
Who told you to come?Quem te mandou vir?
Nada pula, nada entra: Who told, nunca Who did tell.
EFamily E · hide it · escondeLesson 3
A pergunta fica dentro de outra frase: Do you know…? Can you tell me…?
Do you know + what + person + verb
Do you know what she wants me to do?Você sabe o que ela quer que eu faça?
Dentro da frase, ordem de afirmação: what she wants, nunca what does she want.

Toda pergunta tem duas famílias: a letra diz como montar a pergunta, o número é o verb pattern.

Verb patterns · 1 2 3

1 verb + person + to + verb · want, ask, tell, expect, teach

2 let · make · have · help + person + verb · sem to

3 suggest · recommend + that + person + verb · formal
